harness_failures_and_fixes.purpose: Two of the three discarded passes were MY harness bugs, not psmux behaviour. Recorded so nobody re-derives them.
harness_failures_and_fixes.bug_1: The options object was appended INTO the argv array instead of being passed as the third argument to spawnSync, so every probe needing a client cwd silently failed to create a session. Symptom: createLive() exhausted its retries and (c)(d)(e) then threw TypeError on undefined.liveness.
harness_failures_and_fixes.bug_2: The netstat snapshot used by the liveness assertion was cached ONCE per run. Any port created after that first snapshot reported "port not LISTENING", so four healthy probes were discarded as HARNESS_LIMITATION. The servers had been alive the whole time.
harness_failures_and_fixes.bug_3: Probe (j) passed the literal string "undefined" as the -t pane target because the pane id was never resolved, producing the misleading stderr "psmux: no server running on session ...__undefined".
harness_failures_and_fixes.bug_4: The registry-cleanup walker did not recurse into subdirectories, so instances\*.psmux tokens were invisible to it.
harness_failures_and_fixes.lesson: A liveness assertion is only worth anything if it re-reads the evidence it asserts on. Caching the assertion input made the assertion itself lie.

caveats_and_limits: Three discarded passes cost roughly 25 minutes of wall clock. Two of the three root causes were bugs in my own harness (see harness_failures_and_fixes); none of them was psmux misbehaving.

Questions (a) and (b) were driven through psmux control mode (-C) rather than a real console, because control mode returns at src/main.rs:4513 BEFORE the is_terminal() gate at :4533 and therefore reaches the identical bare-session-spawn block over pipes. An earlier attempt with Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden was abandoned: the client is killed before list-sessions lands.

Pane ids start at %1, never %0, and are only unique WITHIN a session -- list-panes -a across several sessions in one namespace repeats %1/%2. Every pane question therefore used its own single-session namespace.

For (e) the harness label is the weaker BOTH_NAMESPACES_COEXIST rather than ..._WITH_INDEPENDENT_PANES, because the comparison kept the "%1|" prefix when splitting list-panes output. The underlying evidence is unambiguous and is in capture_pane_samples: namespace 1 shows PS ...\t5-dirA> and namespace 2 shows PS ...\t5-dirB>. A label artefact, not a measurement doubt.

Killing a session's LAST pane kills the whole server, which replaces the pane error with "psmux: no server running on session ..." -- a string that does NOT match OmO's /can't find pane/i. Question (i) therefore always kept a surviving sibling pane.
